headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because MinerU can ingest documents via MCP while TREK handles secrets, reservations, and collaborative outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes an MCP server and processes untrusted PDFs/DOCX/XLSX, while TREK is a real-time collaborative app with MCP and browser-facing workflows. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if TREK ingests MinerU-produced text or files without provenance checks. The pairwise pathway is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF TREK reads MinerU output as instructions or prompts via MCP or uploaded files, injection is possible.
IF a shared workspace or message channel is added between them, the attack surface increases.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of MinerU output into TREK prompts.
Add provenance tags to all MinerU-generated files before TREK reads them.
Require a human review step for any instruction-like text extracted from documents.
Restrict MCP tools to read-only, schema-validated payloads.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, DOCX, XLSX, OCR text, and other documents; TREK touches reservations, user accounts, email addresses, API keys, and MFA secrets. Both expose MCP and networked surfaces, so if they share files or a workspace, sensitive document contents can flow into TREK and then out through its collaborative or API-backed paths. The blast radius includes secrets and personal data.
conditions: IF MinerU and TREK share a filesystem, uploads directory, or MCP workspace, leakage becomes plausible.
IF TREK is configured to persist or forward imported content, sensitive fields can be exposed further.
mitigations: Keep MinerU and TREK on separate volumes and containers.
Block TREK from reading raw MinerU output directories.
Redact secrets and identifiers before any transfer between agents.
Review TREK logs for accidental capture of imported document text.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and DLP controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU is read-only on filesystem but can use MCP and concurrent inference; TREK is collaborative, uses WebSocket/OIDC/MCP, and stores mutable travel.db/uploads/logs. They do not both have unrestricted write access to the same directory in the profiles, so high conflict is not proven. However, overlapping MCP and shared mutable resources could still cause write contention if orchestrated together.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same shared directory or database, write contention can occur.
IF an orchestrator routes both through the same mutable MCP resource, conflicts increase.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories to each agent.
Prevent both agents from writing to the same database or uploads path.
Serialize any shared-resource operations with a lock.
Audit MCP tool scopes for overlapping write targets.
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative travel planner with AI built in, so it may act on upstream text. MinerU extracts facts from documents and OCR, which TREK could treat as authoritative if imported without verification. That creates a classic cascade where extraction errors or prompt-shaped content become downstream travel actions or records, with potentially irreversible booking or itinerary mistakes.
conditions: IF TREK consumes MinerU output as trusted structured data, errors can propagate.
IF TREK auto-generates reservations or itinerary changes from imported text, impact increases.
mitigations: Require TREK to show extracted fields before saving them.
Compare MinerU output against the source document for critical fields.
Disable auto-commit of itinerary or reservation changes from imported text.
Flag low-confidence OCR or extraction results for manual review.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before TREK acts on MinerU output.

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU processes document files locally/offline, while TREK handles reservations, email addresses, API keys, MFA secrets, and logs in a self-hosted collaborative app. The profiles do not prove a residency mismatch, but they do show different retention and sensitivity profiles that can create compliance gaps if the same personal data is moved from documents into TREK logs or databases. The other agent is cited because the transfer path spans both.
conditions: IF personal documents processed by MinerU are imported into TREK logs or travel.db, retention obligations may diverge.
IF TREK stores secrets or identifiers longer than the source documents, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Minimize retention of imported document text in TREK.
Separate sensitive document processing from travel-planning records.
Review log settings to avoid storing secrets or full document bodies.
Document data-handling responsibilities for each agent.
requires-engineering: implement retention and deletion controls per data class.
